header:
Date: 2027-09-18
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Papertrail), Marcus Holt (SRE Lead), Priya Anand (ML Eng)
summary: Initial discovery for migration from mixed public provider + self-hosted stack (OpenAI + Anthropic + vLLM/TGI). Papertrail is evaluating Hosted for quick lift-and-shift, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data. Main concerns: model parity, prompt/cost regressions, SSO & KMS integration, and realistic perf/cost numbers. Agreed next steps: share benchmarks, security docs, and schedule infra deep dive.
topics: Hosting options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay hi everyone thanks for taking time, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference. we'll do a quick intro and then dig into your stack and goals.
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: Hey Maya, hey Ravi, I'm Lena, CTO at Papertrail. we run a mixed setup today, OpenAI for customer facing features and a couple of in-house vLLM clusters for internal models.
[00:22] Marcus Holt: Marcus here, I look after infra and SRE. we are seeing cost spikes and some concurrency limits on the current setup.
[00:28] Priya Anand: And Priya, ML eng, I own the fine-tuning pipeline and the inference infra for internal models.
[00:35] Ravi Kapoor: Great thanks. quick clarification — when you say vLLM are you running TGI or the HuggingFace/TGI runtime?
[00:43] Priya Anand: It's a mix, we have T G I for our TF-triggered models and direct v-l-l-m for some optimized pipelines, so yeah both.
[00:52] Maya Chen: Cool, that maps to what we see a lot. can you share the main drivers for evaluating a migration? cost, latency, control?
[01:05] Lena Ortiz: All of the above. we want to reduce unit cost for high-volume embeddings and chat, and also have a path to put sensitive models in a VPC or on-prem for a few regulated clients.
[01:16] Marcus Holt: Also reliability — we had a few transient rate-limit outages with the public provider that impacted SLAs.
[01:23] Priya Anand: And parity — we need to make sure outputs match closely; small prompt drift causes large UX regressions.
[01:31] Ravi Kapoor: Understood. a couple of quick questions on scope — are you planning to migrate all models or only some? and do you want a hybrid approach?
[01:40] Lena Ortiz: Hybrid likely. public hosted endpoints for low-friction consumer features, dedicated pools for internal batch/analytics, and private for regulated customers.
[01:49] Maya Chen: That lines up with Redwood's three modes — hosted, dedicated, private. I'll hand over to Ravi to do a technical mapping.
[01:57] Ravi Kapoor: Thanks. Priya, can you describe your current inference pipeline? instance types, batch sizes, kv cache usage, and quantization?
[02:07] Priya Anand: Sure — for the TGI stuff we're usually on p4d-ish GPU equivalents, 8 GPU hosts in a farm. batch sizes vary — for real-time chat we try to keep batch size low to stay under 200ms p95, but batch jobs for rerank/embeddings are larger. most of our models are 16-bit and we do some int8 quant on a subset. kv cache is used for chat, but it's custom in our vllm setup, not standard.
[02:36] Maya Chen: Got it. on the hosting side, are you tied to any specific auth or key management? SSO, SAML, KMS?
[02:44] Marcus Holt: We use Okta for SSO, and AWS KMS for key management. compliance wise we need logs that can be exported into our SIEM and a clear audit trail.
[02:54] Maya Chen: Redwood supports Okta SAML, and we have KMS integrations — we can send the SOC2 pack.
[02:59] Lena Ortiz: Good. what's the realistic effort to prove parity — we have prompt suites and labeled outputs.
[03:07] Ravi Kapoor: We usually run an eval parity suite against your current prompts and models — compute a delta on embeddings and generation metrics. For vLLM/TGI we often run containerized test images that are very close to customer's runtime to reduce differences.
[03:22] Priya Anand: How do you handle tokenizer differences? we have some custom tokenizers for a couple of models.
[03:29] Ravi Kapoor: Tokenizer differences can definitely introduce drift. we try to keep the same tokenizer artifacts, and if necessary we run tokenization normalization in the eval harness. sometimes we include the tokenizer in the container.
[03:40] Maya Chen: also note that our runtime supports prefix/KV caching and continuous batching which helps to lower cost without sacrificing p95 for chat.
[03:48] Lena Ortiz: Can you explain continuous batching? we've heard mixed things — it sounds like a queue that aggregates small requests — how does it impact latency?
[03:58] Ravi Kapoor: In practice it aggregates requests for a few milliseconds using a latency SLO-aware policy. for most chat workloads it adds a few ms but drops the cost per token significantly. if you have hard 100ms p95 targets we can tune the policy or carve out a dedicated, low-latency pool.
[04:20] Marcus Holt: Our target is around 150ms p95 for consumer chat and sub-50ms for embeddings p95. is that realistic?
[04:29] Ravi Kapoor: 150ms p95 is achievable on dedicated pools with optimized kernels and short prompt lengths; embeddings are usually much faster, sub-50ms is doable depending on model size and concurrency.
[04:38] Priya Anand: What's the dev effort to move from our current vLLM containers to Redwood Private?
[04:44] Maya Chen: For Private we provide a control plane and packages for the runtime; customers often need to adapt some init scripts and provide the image or use our recommended images. typical lift is 2-4 weeks for small set of models, more if you have custom infra requirements.
[04:58] Lena Ortiz: We're also worried about vendor lock-in — if we deploy to Redwood Private, can we still run the same containers elsewhere?
[05:06] Ravi Kapoor: Yes, we try to avoid lock-in — our Private option uses standard container images and a consistent API. you can run the same images in your on-prem or other cloud with minimal work. the main value is in the orchestration and observability we provide.
[05:20] Priya Anand: For quantization, do you support int8 and quantization-aware inference? we can't afford large quality drops.
[05:28] Ravi Kapoor: We support multiple quantization profiles and will run quality regressions tied to your eval sets. Redwood Optimize can recommend which models are safe to int8 and which should stay fp16.
[05:38] Marcus Holt: And for compliance customers we need HSM-backed KMS, is that supported?
[05:43] Maya Chen: We integrate with customer KMS and HSM in Private deployments; for Hosted we have encrypted keys and offer per-tenant encryption options but for FIPS/HSM you usually choose Private.
[05:56] Lena Ortiz: About pricing models — is there a hybrid price for Hosted + Dedicated? we have some spiky workloads that could benefit from bursting.
[06:04] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated includes burst and autoscaling options; we can tailor a contract that mixes reserved base capacity and burst credits — we'll share example pricing for your workload.
[06:14] Priya Anand: One technical ask — our current vLLM pipeline relies heavily on long KV caches across multi-turn sessions. will Redwood's runtime preserve KV cache across requests?
[06:26] Ravi Kapoor: Yes, we maintain KV caches and provide mechanisms to pin and reuse caches per-session. there are optimizations for memory and reclamation for large fleets.
[06:36] Lena Ortiz: How would you handle model versioning and rollbacks? we need safe rollouts.
[06:42] Ravi Kapoor: Our Console supports rollouts with canary percentages, auto-fallback policies and time-based rollbacks. we can tie rollouts to your eval metrics so a regression triggers an automatic rollback.
[06:56] Marcus Holt: For the pilot, what do you need from us to run a perf/quality run?
[07:01] Maya Chen: At minimum: model artifacts or pointers, tokenizer, prompt sets and expected outputs, a sample traffic pattern, and access for a temporary perf agent or a peered VPC for Private testing.
[07:14] Priya Anand: We can provide a bucket with models and a small traffic replay. what's the timeframe to get a result?
[07:20] Ravi Kapoor: Typically 5-10 business days from getting artifacts to a first run and results — depends on queue and whether we need to repro tokenizer or retrain quantization.
[07:30] Lena Ortiz: There's a concern about small differences in outputs being amplified in user-facing features — can you measure semantic drift?
[07:38] Ravi Kapoor: We compute embedding distance and generation metrics; for semantic drift we also run downstream metrics like rerank accuracy or classification thresholds you provide.
[07:49] Priya Anand: Do you have any customers who migrated from our exact stack — OpenAI + vLLM/TGI? we'd like references.
[07:57] Maya Chen: We do; I can share 2 anonymized case studies where customers moved critical workloads off a mixture of OpenAI + self-host and saw cost reductions and stable latency.
[08:07] Marcus Holt: On the logging side, we need structured traces per-token for billing reconciliation — can Redwood provide that?
[08:15] Ravi Kapoor: We emit token-level usage and structured logs and traces; you can export them to S3 or a SIEM, and we have tracing hooks for per-request debug.
[08:25] Lena Ortiz: If we decide to pilot, what does the handoff look like?
[08:29] Maya Chen: We normally kick off a sprint-zero: onboarding, baseline benchmark, eval parity, and a perf run. after acceptance we move to a time-boxed pilot on dedicated or private depending on outcome.
[08:40] Priya Anand: Are there any gotchas with TGI — some of our models use custom kernels.
[08:46] Ravi Kapoor: Custom kernels can be supported but may require extra validation. sometimes we build kernel shims or include the kernel in the container. we'll capture that in the compatibility checklist.
[08:58] Maya Chen: Any questions on SLA and uptime targets?
[09:02] Marcus Holt: We need 99.95% availability for customer-facing endpoints and an option for stricter SLOs for enterprise customers.
[09:10] Maya Chen: Dedicated tiers can support 99.95% with contractual SLAs; Private depends on your infra but we provide operational playbooks.
[09:18] Lena Ortiz: How does Redwood handle price transparency — we need per-token cost breakdowns by model and route.
[09:25] Ravi Kapoor: Console has token-level billing, model-level cost, and per-route analytics. we can also provide exportable billing reports.
[09:33] Priya Anand: For embeddings, we have a high volume of small requests. is there a cheaper path than hosted?
[09:39] Ravi Kapoor: Embeddings are often cheaper on Dedicated or Private because of batch amortization and optimized kernels; we can model this in the benchmark.
[09:48] Marcus Holt: Security question again — do you support customer-managed logging and retention policies?
[09:54] Maya Chen: Yes, retention, log exports, and your SIEM ingestion are supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can export but with more restrictions.
[10:03] Lena Ortiz: Ok can you walk through a sample timeline for a pilot lasting 6 weeks?
[10:09] Maya Chen: Week 1: onboarding and artifact handoff. Weeks 2-3: parity eval and perf runs. Week 4: iterate on quant/ker nel/profile. Week 5: pilot traffic with canary. Week 6: review and go/no-go.
[10:25] Priya Anand: That seems reasonable. I want a more technical meeting focused on vLLM/TGI compatibility — can we schedule that with your SEs and our infra?
[10:33] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we'll set up a technical deep dive with Ravi and our infra engineering.
[10:38] Ravi Kapoor: For the deep dive please also include someone familiar with your custom kernels and your container build pipeline.
[10:45] Marcus Holt: We'll have our infra lead join. for the perf run we prefer to do it in our account with a peered agent if possible.
[10:53] Maya Chen: We can support peered runs; we'll include instructions for a temp perf agent.
[10:58] Lena Ortiz: Anything else — latency, cost, security, parity are the main things.
[11:03] Maya Chen: Great, recap: we'll send the benchmark template, SOC2/ISO pack, and a compatibility checklist. we'll schedule the SE deep dive and aim to start the parity run once we have artifacts.
[11:14] Priya Anand: Timeline to start the deep dive?
[11:17] Maya Chen: We can do it next week — I'll propose slots.
[11:20] Marcus Holt: Sounds good.
[11:22] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and action items.
[11:26] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, bye.
[11:28] (call ends)
